messages.subject: Inquiring about glyphs
parts:
Originally I sent this as an email (containing 2 questions) directly to Hadley who requested I send them to the ggplot help list as separate questions (this is question 2):


I love ggplot2, particularly the faceting (facet_grid) which lattice can do but with much less flexibility and intuition.  I've been working on a for fun project using state school assessment data and mapping it using ggplot2 as faceted chorolopleths (
http://www.talkstats.com/showthread.php/23324-An-R-learning-project-(feel-free-to-learn-with-me)?p=82365&viewfull=1#post82365 ).   I came across a similar map that has pie graphs plotted on it, at the same time I checked out Wilkinson's "The Grammar of Graphics" as a certain package maker cites this book as inspiration.  I now know what I was seeing was what Wilkinson calls glyphs.  I asked about doing this type of plotting on a map on stackoverflow (
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/10368180/plotting-pie-graphs-on-map-in-ggplot ).   The folks there didn't have a means of plotting them using ggplot but did provide some info which indicates of your possible intention to add glyphs to ggplot2 at some point (the paper baptise links to).  

Is this a possibility, intention etc. for the future?

Thanks,Tyler Rinker
